sm: This is the opening of Truth Hunters, a modern day parable read aloud. It begins with questions about whether God wants people to seek the truth and what that takes. Then the story starts. A girl named Onika practices with a wooden sword in her backyard in the wasteland, preparing for the gathering, the only way to join the truth hunters and earn a real sword. Her father warns that it is dangerous. A thorny, snarling vine creature seizes her and drags her away. In the next chapter, two servants named Mass and Thrope bring more recruits to the accuser, their chained master.

The accuser, furious, demands to know why people keep trying to join the truth hunters. He wants everyone content at home with no thought of the gathering, since the truth hunters expose the truth about the world and the return of the king. He throws a toad-like creature called a variant against a wall, then orders his henchmen to make an offer to the captives or lock them up. Onika wakes in a dark cell with three other kids, Val, Jenny and Chase. They believe they are in the adversaries' fortress. Val says the adversaries cannot truly hurt them if they stand firm. Onika hears scratching sounds beneath the floor.

Mass and Thrope visit the cell and mock the children, claiming the truth hunters only give false hope and that the accuser's world is paradise. They offer freedom if the children join them, and promise to move them to the real dungeon by morning. The children refuse. They search for a way out, trying stones, bars, a hairpin and a pocket knife, all without success. Val offers to hold the guards while the others flee, but the others insist on sticking together. Onika keeps hearing the noise growing louder. Finally the floor cracks open, and something bursts through the stones.

The creature is a friendly dog who licks Val's face. He has dug a tunnel, and the children crawl through it, with Val reluctant but unwilling to be left behind. They emerge on a narrow ledge high on a cliff above a river. The dog bounds down the cliff but the children cannot follow. A foul smell of rotting meat and green vapor, and thin vines, come out of the tunnel. Chase and Jenny jump into the river. Onika is too frightened until Val grabs her and leaps. The dog follows them.

The children survive the fall and rest on the riverbank. The dog leads them through the woods to an old stone forge. The armorer, a grumpy blacksmith, makes plows and says they are more useful than swords. He calls the dog K9 and feeds the hungry children bread, ham and cold goat milk. He tells them they are real truth hunters who simply came the hard way, though they lack training. He explains that the only way back is through the adversaries. He sends them to sleep in the loft and tells them they will talk tomorrow.

The armorer says it is no use asking more questions that night, and the children go to sleep in the loft. Then the accuser rages at Mass and Thrope for letting the children escape, blaming the dog, who digs through every trap. Thrope suggests using the variants, creatures that frighten inexperienced truth hunters. The accuser grudgingly agrees, though he insists they must not be allowed to follow the variants. He says fear that has been overcome helps the truth hunters, not the adversaries. Mass begins herding the variants out of the room.

In the morning the armorer hurries the children outside and hands each a swords. They are useless looking: rusty, tarred, or just a bladeless hilt. He says they can defeat the accuser with them, but they need training from the forerunners, who are not far away. He tells them to follow the marked path, stay on it no matter how it looks, and keep using their swords. The path will be occupied by adversaries like Thrope and Mass, but nothing can stop them if they keep moving. After some debate, the children decide to seek the forerunners first.

The four children agree to get training first, though Onika would rather wait behind. K9 leads them into the forest, where the symbol of the truth hunters grows right out of the trees. Val leads, worrying over his bladeless sword. Jenny's sword keeps oozing tar. At a meadow, five paths lead through different landscapes, and each bears the symbol. Val proposes taking the hardest path first, the rocky one, and Chase agrees after Jenny asks him to stick together. They walk into a canyon, grow tired, and sit on rocks that seem to appear just for them.

The children fall asleep on the comfortable rocks and wake hours later with their feet aching. They hear a rumble that sounds like laughter. The canyon grows bitter, with a foul stream and bubbling mud. Odd toad-like variants hop on the hillside, attack each other, and begin following them. The stream disappears into a small hole in a rock wall. Then part of the wall crumbles and opens an easier path, and Val wants to take it. Onika notes the symbol is over the stream. The variants close in, and they flee into the new canyon, with K9 following reluctantly.

In the new canyon the path gets worse, with mold and stagnant pools. A variant is chewing Jenny's sword. More variants burst from the water and chase them. Mass appears as a face in the rock wall and closes the canyon with boulders. The children scramble back over the rocks, then must crawl into the cave where the stinking stream enters. K9 fights the variants to save Onika, and disappears under a swarm of them. The children crawl through the cave, with the others helping Onika.

They fear K9 is dead and Val blames himself. In the cave the water glows and smells awful. Onika tastes it and says it is sweet, and her mouth glows. One by one they drink, and it refreshes them. They walk without tiring and emerge into sunlight, far sooner than expected. They find a creek, a mine-like cave and a dwelling, with the symbol on a rock in the stream. Nobody seems to be home, and Onika wanders among the digging tools.

They find dirt flying out of a pit and meet a man called Dugout, who jumps out brandishing a shovel until he sees their swords. He is the forerunner, digging up an ancient city that the accuser would like hidden. He says the accuser hides evidence from before the rift and denies it, so Dugout keeps digging out the truth. He shows them the mine, with mosaics and bathhouses. Onika, wary of the adversaries, asks to stay and help him dig. He says adversaries cannot attack the truth directly, only sneak and trap people. He offers them dinner and a bed.

After dinner and a night's sleep, Dugout taps each sword with his shovel, which sharpens them. He tells them truth hunters keep moving. A variant hops by and Dugout knocks it away, saying the variants are not really harmful and that it might be interesting to follow them sometime. He doubts that K9 is dead. Onika begs to stay, but he tells her she is using curiosity to hide from fear and must face her fears first. They are told to move forward, and the path returns them to the crossroads. They choose the path through the grain, with Val leading.

In the grain field the path winds monotonously and each child thinks privately. Chase resents Val giving orders. Jenny worries about their disunity. Val worries about protecting them, especially Onika. Onika wonders why she is afraid. Then she asks whether they are still on the right path, and no one has seen a symbol for a long time. The grain shifts and closes the path behind them, and a hissing laugh reveals Thrope is toying with them. They wander as the path keeps changing.

Onika, furious, charges and slashes down the grain, and underneath the fallen stalks they find the symbol, which Thrope had been hiding. Black birds attack in waves, and the children first run, then stand and fight together, slashing at both grain and birds. Onika holds her ground against a swarm and survives with scratches. They follow the symbols and break out of the grain field. Ahead stands a glazed stone dome beside two pools. Onika faints from exhaustion and wakes in the dome's cool interior.

Onika wakes to meet Dr. Auger, the forerunner, a cheerful man with a streak of white hair and a cloak lined with scrolls. He says defeating the accuser is not yet done, then corrects himself, as he sometimes disremembers. Along a hallway of desks stand clocks counting down to events. The last one chimes just as the children arrive, and dinner is ready. He explains the king's oracles tell what will happen, whereas the king's chronicles tell what has already happened. The oracles are always true, though he doesn't know everything.

Dr. Auger explains that the accuser will certainly be defeated, but the children will defeat him only if they stay on the path and keep seeking truth, since promises involving people often carry an if. Jenny talks with him privately about how her friends dislike her pointing out their faults. He says truth is like bread: forced on someone, it only hurts, but offered as a choice it is good. The next day the children start up the vine jungle path, with Chase hacking at vines after Dr. Auger sharpens their swords. They notice slidey frogs marked with the symbol.

After Dr. Auger sharpens their swords with an oracle, the children start down the vine jungle path, and Chase leads for the first time at Jenny's suggestion. The vines wall off the path, so Chase hacks at them, soaking in sweat, while the vines keep growing back. Animals begin to appear, including butterflies, lizards and insects. Onika spots a slimy frog-like creature with the truth hunter symbol on its back, and the creatures all travel the same direction as the path. Her hand ends up covered in slick oil. Chase finally exhausts himself and nearly falls, and Val and Jenny insist the group take shifts.

Val, Jenny and Onika each take a turn chopping, and Jenny squeals every time a slidey frog darts past. Chase takes his turn determined not to tire, and falls into a focused rhythm so deep that he stops hearing the others. Onika watches the frogs and tests their oil. Thrope's thorny vines silently snatch Val and Jenny, and then Onika, and drag them into the tangle. Chase turns around and finds no one there. He spots a shoe, hacks toward it, and sees Onika's eyes, furious, darting toward the frogs. He understands and pushes a frog into her hand.

Onika bursts from the vines coated in frog slime, and shows Chase that the oil lets them slip through the vines. Val, Jenny and Onika escape, with Onika threatening Thrope. The group covers themselves in frog oil and swims through the vines, following the frogs. They find a round building with a glass dome and a giant telescope. A steel door opens by itself, closes behind them, and lights come on in a tunnel. A voice from a trumpet-shaped tube asks what they want and which forerunner they seek.

The voice says they need a bath, and the building whisks each child through cleaning jets and dryers. They land clean on beanbag chairs. They meet Silah, a forerunner in a green lab coat and spinning goggles, who scans them. She giggles, easily forgets things when focused, and has automated her workshop to remind her. She serves dinner as mush, saying she removes texture and appearance because she eats only for nutrition. Her remark about getting too focused makes Chase remember how he nearly cost the group by chopping alone.

Silah says she studies everything the king created to learn about him. She shows them her telescope, which looks both outward to the stars and inward to the details of a vine. She says the closer you look, the more you find the king's fingerprints, not the accuser's. The scope strengthens their swords, and Val can now see a faint blade. The lab puts them to bed through tubes. Chase sneaks back to the scope room hoping to look at the path or the accuser. Silah finds him and warns that too much focus can make you forget what matters most.

Silah finishes telling Chase that focus can mislead if it distracts from what is most important. Then the accuser rages at Mass and Thrope and decides to go himself next time. The children take the path through the rolling hills, which is easy, and Val wonders why no danger comes. At a fork with no symbol, they choose the easy right path over the gloomy wood. They enter the wood anyway after finding the symbol, hear howling in the mist, and are tackled by K9, alive. They come to a raging river at a cliff, with a tree far across.

The river is impassable. Val wants to go back and try the other fork, while Chase and Onika argue the symbol was right. Val sets off alone to look for directions, and K9 slips away to follow him. Val meets an old man at a cabin, roasting turnips. K9 growls. The man's smoke makes Val sleepy, and the man says one path is as good as another and urges him to rest inside. Val feels drowsy and lets himself be led toward the door.

K9 bites Val's ankle, waking him, and the disguise melts away. The old man is the accuser. Val slashes at him with his sword and flees through the woods with K9. Meanwhile at the river, Chase, Jenny and Onika wait and worry. A flood of variants pours out of the woods and swarms them. The variants cannot really hurt them, but they knock them around. Onika notices some variants hopping over the cliff edge and remembers Dugout's hint. They find a hidden path down the cliff.

The three follow the variants along the path behind the waterfall and back up onto the far side, near the tree. Val bursts out of the woods behind them, finds the river empty and his friends gone, and fears the variants carried them off. Something large crashes through the trees behind him. K9 swims into the river and signals Val to follow. The current knocks Val under, but he stabs his sword into the bedrock, which makes a calm pocket of water. He crosses by stabbing and leaping. The friends reunite and apologize. They find the great tree.

The children arrive at a dwelling woven from three intertwined trees, and are welcomed by the forerunner, the Crimson Cord. He feeds them and listens as they tell their story. He says Coda, the final forerunner, is almost unreachable unless they work together. Onika notices a crimson ribbon running through the grain of every room. In the morning he shows them a glowing crimson sphere, the nexus, the thread of the king through his creation. He passes it around their swords, making visible a cord that binds them together. He says they will need it to reach Coda.

Chase asks what the Crimson Cord means. He says some barriers can only be overcome by unity of spirit and purpose, and the next journey will be their final test before facing the accuser. He will not say more, but tells them they are already prepared if they put into practice what they have learned. Val realizes they have help beyond themselves. They set off toward Coda over an easy path and reach a sheer cliff with a symbol in the rock. Val asks them to work together, not orders, and they begin climbing by driving their swords into the stone.

Climbing, Onika loses her footing when a foothold vanishes, but the crimson cord between her sword and Jenny's catches her. They develop a method of swinging Onika upward, and Mass and Thrope try to stop them with disappearing footholds, spikes and grasping vines. Onika slashes through a vine. At the top they swing Onika over the edge, then pull the others up one by one. They collapse, laughing and teasing. They see a spotless ancient castle, and a swift shape twirls on its battlements.

The shape leaps down and defeats all four, knocking the swords from their hands. It is Coda, who pins Val's throat with her sword but stops when he says they are truth hunters seeking her. She tells them never to let their swords be taken. She notes that their swords now gleam, and says they are ready to face the accuser now. Val admits he does not feel ready to lead, but she says leading is listening, serving and, if necessary, sacrificing. She takes them along the wall of the king's fastness, which stands across from the accuser's fortress.

Coda explains the king's fastness stands in plain view so that all who see the accuser's lies can see the truth, and it will stand until the king heals the rift. She lowers them to the path and tells them to hold to their swords and to each other. As they near the accuser's fortress, Mass and Thrope ambush them, hurling stones and vines. The four fight them, and Onika slips between Mass's legs. They retreat and regroup, and Chase smells the rotting stench. The accuser floats through the iron gate, his chains clanking, and attacks them with claws.

The accuser slashes the four, but when they stand back to back his dodging is limited. Mass and Thrope throw rocks and try to herd them toward the gate and a trap. Onika notices a small door guarded by a chained variant. Val sends Chase to the door while the others cover him, and Onika follows to help. Chase frees and bats the variant at Mass, and he and Onika trip the henchmen with the cord between their swords. K9 arrives with a stampede of variants that bury the two henchmen. Val and Jenny keep fighting the accuser.
